title: Tool Calling, Spring Style
objective: After this lesson you will be able to expose POJO methods as tools, operate ToolCallingAdvisor auto-registration (ordering, disabling, user control), and scope tools per call with context passing.
why: Agents act through tools, and Spring AI's story is idiomatic: plain methods become model-callable with framework-managed execution loops. The mechanics that matter — auto-registration defaults, advisor ordering inside/outside loops, user-controlled execution for UIs — decide whether tools behave transparently or mysteriously in production services.

blocks.text: Plain methods with `@Tool` annotations register via `.tools(new OrderTools())` or `defaultTools(...)`: descriptions steer selection, signatures constrain args, return values feed the loop. No framework base classes, no XML — methods you already write, annotated. Tool design (naming, sibling disambiguation, closed shapes) carries over whole from LangGraph Ch.7 and MCP courses.

The advisor auto-registers **unless**: globally disabled (`spring.ai.chat.client.tool-calling.enabled=false`), per-call disabled (`AdvisorParams.toolCallingAdvisorAutoRegister(false)`), or superseded (your own ToolAdvisor present). Disable globally when tools must never auto-fire (all calls user-driven); per-call when streaming intermediates to UIs; custom builder bean for manager-level control. Each mode tested, never assumed.
Ordering: inside vs outside the loop

The `advisor-order` property positions repetition: value **below** advisors that must repeat per iteration (RAG refresh each loop), **above** those running once per request (audit logging). Default suits the common case; custom loops need explicit ordering with the inside/outside decision recorded. Misordered advisors execute at wrong cadence silently — the setting to check first when loops behave oddly.

blocks.title: Place the advisor
blocks.note: Run it: expect memory,rag,tools then tools,audit (audit ranked outside/after the loop, running once per request). Order positions repetition: inside-loop advisors repeat per iteration, outside run once per request.

items: POJO @Tool methods + .tools(): framework-managed loops, zero base classes
Auto-registration controlled globally/per-call/custom-builder; user-controlled execution for UI streaming
advisor-order positions repetition (inside) vs once (outside); misordering fails silently

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice orderer on both inputs and explain audit-last. (b) Write the disable matrix (global/per-call/custom-builder) with one use case each. (c) State what breaks if audit logging runs inside the tool loop, in one sentence.
hints: Orders: memory,rag,tools then audit,tools — audit outside (once per request) by rank.
Global: all-manual shops; per-call: UI streaming intermediates; custom-builder: manager-level control (documented wiring).
Audit-inside duplicates log entries per iteration (noise + cost) and misattributes single decisions as repeated ones.
exercise.why: Ordering semantics (repetition positioning), disable granularity (control levels), and audit placement (once-per-request) are the three tool-loop judgments.
exercise.code: // Advisor-order pattern: inside-loop vs outside documented per advisor.

quiz.q: Tools sent to model but never execute. Cause + fix?
options: Auto-registration disabled (property/per-call/custom-supersede) — re-enable or drive user-controlled execution explicitly
quiz.explain: Definitions without execution means the loop advisor is off. Re-enable deliberately or own the loop with user-controlled execution.

quiz.q: Audit log shows every decision 5x. Cause?
options: Audit advisor ordered inside the tool loop — move outside (higher order value) for once-per-request logging
quiz.explain: Repetition follows order values: inside-loop advisors repeat per iteration. Audit belongs outside unless per-iteration detail is the point.

quiz.q: Streaming intermediates to a UI while tools run. Setup?
options: Per-call disable auto-registration + user-controlled loop: observe each iteration, forward chunks, drive explicitly
quiz.explain: User-controlled execution exists for observable loops: disable auto, drive manually, stream deliberately. The documented UI pattern.

summary: POJO tools, controlled auto-registration, ordered repetition, user-driven loops when UIs demand. Tool mechanics verified against the 2.0.1 reference.
